step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents Micamai's web application boilerplate solution hosted on AWS. The main application stack consists of CloudFront delivering static assets stored in S3, and an ALB routing web requests to containerized workloads running on ECS. The ECS cluster interacts with three persistence services: OpenSearch (Elasticsearch) for full-text search, ElastiCache for in-memory caching, and RDS for relational data storage. The continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) section uses CodePipeline to automate docker image builds deposited into ECR, while CloudFormation provisions infrastructure and triggers zero-downtime deployments onto ECS.

graph.name: Micamai Web Application Boilerplate Architecture
graph.notes: A standardized, highly scalable, and secure AWS infrastructure boilerplate built with Ansible and CloudFormation templates for web and mobile projects.

nodes.name: RDS

nodes.name: ECS

nodes.name: CLOUDFRONT
nodes.notes: Global CDN distribution offering DDoS protection and static asset caching.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores static content and assets served via CloudFront.

nodes.name: ALB

nodes.name: ECR
nodes.notes: Elastic Container Registry holding Docker images generated by CodeBuild.

nodes.name: CODEPIPELINE
nodes.notes: Orchestrates CI/CD pipeline triggered by repository pushes.

nodes.name: CLOUDFORMATION
nodes.notes: Manages infrastructure templates and executes automated deployments to ECS.

edges.notes: CloudFront fetches and serves static web assets from S3 bucket.
ALB routes web requests to containerized applications in ECS.
ECS tasks query Elasticsearch for search queries.
ECS tasks read and write data to ElastiCache.
ECS tasks read and persist business data in RDS.
CodePipeline executes build steps and stores generated Docker images in ECR.
CloudFormation triggers zero-downtime container deployments onto ECS.
